question.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Limit at Infinity: Infinite Solutions
question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{{x}^{3}+1}{2{x}^{2}+x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{{x}^{3}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{x}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(x+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})}{(2+\frac{1}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{(x+0)}{(2+0)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\,\,\frac{x}{2} \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
